1
The table shows some physical quantities.
Which row correctly identifies the quantities as scalars or vectors?
acceleration
charge
kinetic energy
wavelength
A
scalar
vector
vector
scalar
B
vector
vector
scalar
scalar
C
scalar
scalar
scalar
vector
D
vector
scalar
scalar
scalar

hints: Start with acceleration: it is defined from change in velocity, so ask whether a direction is needed to describe it fully.
Link kinetic energy to $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$: speed is squared so only magnitude matters, unlike velocity.
Check charge and wavelength: charge is described by amount and sign in coulombs, and wavelength is a length in $\text{m}$, with no vector direction required.
walkthrough: Recall the test: a vector has magnitude and direction, while a scalar has magnitude only.
Acceleration is $a = \Delta v / \Delta t$, where velocity change $\Delta v$ has direction, so acceleration must also have direction and is a vector.

Charge $Q$ is measured in coulombs with a value and positive or negative sign, and kinetic energy $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ depends on speed squared, so both are fully described by magnitude and are scalars.
Wavelength $\lambda$ is the distance between two adjacent crests, measured in $\text{m}$, so it is a scalar even though the wave travels in a direction.
Only the row with vector, scalar, scalar, scalar matches all four quantities. This is option D

A.explanation: Acceleration is not a scalar and kinetic energy is not a vector, so this row reverses both.

B.explanation: Acceleration is correctly a vector, but charge is a scalar with magnitude and sign only, not direction.

C.explanation: Charge and kinetic energy are scalars, but acceleration needs a direction and wavelength is a distance, so both are mislabelled here.

D.explanation: Acceleration is a vector, while charge, kinetic energy and wavelength have magnitude only and are scalars.
